Thanks Rafael — good call today. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying questions so we can move to sizing: 

- Deployment preference: we want dedicated capacity (reserved) in the US region. We are not ready for a full private VPC/on-prem deployment yet, but data needs to stay in US-only regions.
- Production target: average 40 TPS sustained; peak bursts to ~120 TPS for short windows (5–10m).
- Concurrency: expect ~50 concurrent users/streams on average, peaks to ~200 during launches.
- Token mix: prompts average ~120 tokens, generation average ~600 tokens; ~10% of requests spike to 2k+ tokens.
- Models: leaning toward larger open models (Llama-family / 34B–70B) or your curated model variants. We care about latency (<400ms p50 for short chats, tolerance for p95 up to 1s depending on seq length).

Questions: 
1) For our token mix and peaks, do you recommend A100 or H100?
2) Rough ballpark on number of cards/nodes for 40 TPS sustained with our token mix (we know exact numbers depend on model/quantization).
3) Any data you need from our side (logs, sample payloads) to produce a firm estimate?

Can we do a sizing workshop next week? Thanks — Samir

Samir — thanks for the clear summary and the call earlier. +1 on a sizing workshop. Quick answers and next steps below.

Answers / notes:
- Deployment: Dedicated in US region is fully supported; we can keep data residency constraints and provide audit logs. Private VPC is an option later if you need customer-managed networking.
- GPU recommendations (short): H100 tends to give the best perf for long-token generation and high-throughput, but availability/cost can favor A100 for predictable pricing. We often recommend H100 for heavy gen workloads; A100 is reasonable if you want lower cost per card and are willing to run more cards.
- Ballpark: with your token mix (120 prompt / 600 generation avg) and 40 TPS sustained, I'd estimate somewhere in the 3–6 H100 card range (or 5–9 A100 cards) depending on model family and quantization. This is very rough — we'll refine in the workshop.

What we need from you to produce a firm sizing: 
- 7-day traffic extract (per-minute TPS or RPS) and peak windows
- Sample payloads (prompt lengths, example requests) or a small set of logs
- Preferred model(s) and whether you plan to use int8/quantized variants or fp16/float models

I've attached our dedicated sizing template to collect the above and included a short estimate doc with our assumptions.

Samir — quick technical follow-up from our side with a few concrete ballparks so you have something to plan against before the workshop. 

Given the mix you described (120 prompt / 600 gen avg; 40 TPS sustained; 120 TPS burst):
- If you plan to run a 34B-class open model (quantized int8): ~1 H100 can handle ~8–12 TPS for long generations; so 4 H100s is a reasonable starting point for 40 TPS with headroom. For 70B-class models you should expect ~40–60% fewer TPS per card; plan for ~1.6–2x more capacity.
- For A100s we typically see ~60–75% of H100 perf on these workloads, so expect ~1.5–2x the number of A100 cards compared to H100.
- Concurrency: you mentioned ~50 avg concurrent sessions. Make sure your routing/batching settings use session affinity where needed. Also consider KV/prefix caching to reduce repeated prefix compute on conversational workloads.

Notes/assumptions:
- These numbers assume quantized model variants where applicable (int8). Floating point models increase memory and reduce per-card TPS.
- We assumed average generation length of 600 tokens; 10% of requests at 2k tokens will increase steady-state load on memory bandwidth and may require additional headroom.

Attached a short estimate PDF with the math and a link to our sizing workbook. If you can share a 7-day RPS CSV we can run the exact calc and come back with a recommended cluster layout (cards, nodes, and expected p50/p95 latencies).

Proposed workshop: Tue Apr 20 11:00–12:30 PT — Rafael, Samir, Aditya, and 1 infra/ML engineer from Acme. I'll prepare the model mapping and a couple of cluster layouts (A100 vs H100) for discussion.
